title: Latency divergence guardrail and rolling net-health smoother for tier-aware region decider
creator: Ana Patel
description:
Problem: We observe short-lived region outages and high-p95 spikes that are not captured by our current region score (which primarily averages p95 across long windows). This causes client-facing latency degradations and noisy failovers. Goal: implement a guardrail that detects percentile divergence (p95 vs p50) and correlates it with a smoothed network-health signal to make region selection more robust for tiered traffic (gold/silver/beta).

Proposed approach:
1) Telemetry windows: maintain 1m/5m/15m sliding windows for p50 and p95 per region and per model-variant. Compute two signals: percentile_gap = p95 - p50 and divergence_ratio = p95 / max(p50, 1ms). Compute delta over 1m->5m to detect sudden surges.
2) Rolling net-health smoother: ingest network signals (packet-loss, TCP retransmit rate, infra 5xx rate, control-plane errors). Produce a single nethealth_score in [0,100] using an EWMA with a conservative alpha (0.15) and an anomaly attenuator that temporarily reduces alpha when a single outlier spike is detected (to avoid noisy flip-flops). Implement hysteresis: health must exceed threshold for 3 consecutive windows to be considered recovered.
3) Guardrail decision: if divergence_ratio > X (configurable, default 3.0) AND nethealth_score < Y (configurable, default 65), mark region as degraded_for_latency. Degraded regions remain eligible for limited traffic only under slow-open staging (1% -> 10% -> 50%).
4) Tier-aware penalties: apply tier multipliers to the guardrail. Gold traffic has lower tolerance (lower X, higher Y) and will failover sooner; silver/beta get larger ramp windows. This preserves SLAs while avoiding full-pop evacuation for transient blips.
5) Fallback model variants: when a region is degraded_for_latency, routing should prefer compatible model variants that are lower-cost/shorter-latency (e.g., quantized or smaller-fp variant) if available. If the model variant switch is unavailable or quality regression is unacceptable, traffic uses cross-region fallback with priority to regions with low divergence_ratio.
6) Observability & audit: router api returns reason_codes and scoring_breakdown (p50, p95, divergence_ratio, nethealth_score, tier_penalty) for every decision and emits traces to tracing system. Dashboards and alerts include composite SLO breach signals based on p95 across gold traffic and cross-region fallback counts.

Implementation notes:
- Compute signals in the telemetry aggregator (ingest path) and expose via short-lived redis cache for the region-decider process. Avoid making routing decisions depend on long RPC chains.
- Configurable knobs: divergence_ratio_threshold, gap_ms_threshold, nethealth_threshold, recovery_windows, slow_open_ramps. Keep defaults conservative and gate behind feature flag (route.guardrails.divergence_v1).
- Add unit/e2e tests for synthetic spike scenarios (p95-only spike, symmetric spike, packet-loss-only).
- Backfill and replay historical telemetry for tuning thresholds using last 90 days.

Success metrics (how we’ll measure):
- Reduce gold-tier p95 tail breaches caused by single-region issues by 40% in 30 days after rollout.
- Reduce full-pop region evacuations for transient anomalies by 60%.
- Maintain <2% false-positive degradations across historical replay.

Rollout plan:
Stage 0 - feature flag off: telemetry-only (expose signals and dashboards). Monitor for 5d. (Owner: Marcus)
Stage 1 - dry-run: route-decider computes decisions and logs but does not change traffic. Enable in canary region. Run 48h. (Owner: Marcus)
Stage 2 - constrained ramp: enable slow-open staging for beta/silver, gold still dry-run. 1% -> 10% -> 50% over 72h if no regressions. (Owner: Marcus + SE oncall)
Stage 3 - full enable: apply to all tiers. Disable only behind incident-runbook.

Runbooks & fallback: document steps for operator to force region back online, to clear EWMA cache, and to revert to baseline scoring. Link runbook in links below.

Engineering trade-offs considered:
- Aggressiveness vs availability: lowering thresholds reduces p95 breaches but increases risk of unnecessary fallback; using hysteresis and slow-open mitigates this.
- Computation locality: placing smoothing in ingest reduces routing latency but adds complexity to the telemetry pipeline.
- Variant fallback quality: switching model variants can impact output quality; we restrict automatic variant fallbacks to variants marked as "quality-equivalent" in the model catalog or to use-canary flag.
